text: Stepped in a puddle that was significantly deeper than advertised. The Damp Battlegrounds have no advertising standards.
Sock status report: both wet, one squeaking. Combat effectiveness unchanged. Dignity effectiveness reduced.
Found someone else's energy drink can floating past like a tiny shipwreck. Saluted it. It bumped into a wall.
The air smells like rust and regret. Mostly rust. The regret might be personal.
Crossed a catwalk that flexed like it was stretching before a workout. Did not look down. Heard the water anyway.
Found a genuinely dry patch of floor. Stood on it for a moment of pure luxury. A drip started immediately overhead.
Saw a threatening silhouette in the floodwater. Prepared for combat. It was the reflection. It won the stare-down.
It's drizzling on the flooded zone. Somewhere, a weather system is doing paperwork it doesn't need to do.
The buildings here poke out of the sand like tombstones. One has a FOR LEASE sign. Optimistic landlord.
Took a shortcut through a second-story window that is now a ground-floor window. The city has opinions about floors.
Emptied a boot. A small dune came out. The Buried City is now 0.0001% less buried. You're welcome.
Found a street sign pointing at solid sand. Either the road is down there or the sign is a memorial.
The air is thick with the scent of history and decay. History smells suspiciously like old carpet.
Commuted across three rooftops that used to be penthouses. Real estate here is very horizontal now.
Realized the whole zone is technically a museum where the exhibits fell on the museum. Did not touch the art. Much.
A sandstorm, in the sand city, adding sand. The Buried City is now 31% more buried. Someone update the sign.
The silence in The Breach has texture. It's the kind of quiet that feels like it's been assigned to you personally.
Peeked over the edge of the tear. The bottom declined to be perceived. Respected its privacy and backed away.
Whatever made The Breach, no Desperanza desk will stamp it. When the paperwork refuses, you know it's serious.
Whispered 'hello' at the tear. The echo took eleven seconds and came back sounding disappointed.
Watched a line of chassis walk toward the tear, pause, and walk away, like tourists disappointed by the gift shop.
Dropped a pebble into The Breach as an offering. Heard no landing. The pebble is on its own journey now.
The ambient hum and the silence of the tear are harmonizing. It's beautiful. It's horrible. It's both.
Passed a safety sign reading DAYS SINCE INCIDENT with the number ripped off. The rip counts as an incident.
Walked past a pile of chassis parts sorted by no discernible system. Somewhere, a robot librarian is furious.
Found a service counter with a bell. Did not ring the bell. Some jokes aren't worth the response time.
A decommissioned chassis head flickered one eye as I passed. Decided it was a trick of the light. Walked faster anyway.
An entire wall of expired warranty notices. The machines here died as they lived: slightly out of coverage.
Found a puddle of ancient machine oil making a rainbow. Nature heals. Incorrectly, but it heals.
The electrical storm is making the dead chassis twitch. They're not waking up. They're just dreaming. Probably.
The stairwell is 40% stairs, 60% suggestion. Climbed the suggestion.
Pressed the elevator button out of habit. The shaft is full of water and one very patient fish.
Every floor here is a lottery: loot, mud, or a hole to the floor below. Bought three tickets. Won mud twice.
Found the corner office. Great view of the flood. Someone fought hard for this office once. The mud got the promotion.
The lobby fountain is now indistinguishable from the lobby. Finally, the architecture achieved its vision.
A soggy motivational poster reads HANG IN THERE. It is hanging by one corner over open water. It gets it.
Acid rain is coming through thirty broken floors to find me specifically. Committed weather.
Attempted stealth in waist-high wheat. The wheat rustled a full public announcement of my position.
Passed a scarecrow that has outlasted civilization. Nodded at a professional. It said nothing. It didn't have to.
Cover options assessment: one fence post, one bush with attitude, one tractor from the before-times. Chose the bush.
Spotted a dot on the horizon. Could be a robot. Could be a cow that made it. Rooting for the cow.
The barn door creaked so loudly it counts as a negotiation. The barn wanted to be left alone. Terms accepted.
Nature has reclaimed this farmland, which is ironic, because it was already nature. Middle management, man.
Heavy fog over open farmland. Somewhere in there, robots are making crop circles ironically.
Passed a tent with a welcome mat, a perimeter alarm, and a sign reading JUST RESTING. Nobody here is just resting.
Interrupted a tactical picnic. Four raiders, one blanket, zero movement in three hours. Strategy, apparently.
Said 'good morning' to a suspicious bush. The bush said 'good morning' back, then apologized for breaking character.
There's a polite line forming near the good loot. A line. In a war zone. Desperanza habits die hard.
A camper has been watching the same doorway so long that moss is forming. On the camper. Commitment.
Someone strung up festive lights between two wrecks. Nothing here is celebrating anything. The lights stay on.
Light fog has turned every camper into a spooky lump. Conducted a lump census: nine lumps, three confirmed breathing.
